extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants preparing proposals for the CDMRP Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program (PRCRP) FY24 funding opportunity
extracted.subtask_description: Lists the FY24 PRCRP topic areas that proposals may address and the statutory exclusions/definitions that determine whether a research application is within scope for funding. Useful for applicants to determine topic fit/eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: FY24 PRCRP Topic Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The FY24 PRCRP Topic Areas are the specific cancer types and categories the program will accept for FY24 funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FY24 PRCRP Topic Areas (eligible topics) are: Bladder cancer; Blood cancers; Brain cancer (except glioblastoma); Colorectal cancer; Endometrial cancer; Esophageal cancer; Germ cell cancers; Liver cancer; Lymphoma; Mesothelioma; Metastatic cancers; Myeloma; Neuroblastoma; Pediatric, adolescent, and young adult cancers; Pediatric brain tumors; Sarcoma; Stomach cancer; Thyroid cancer. Applicants should target their research to one or more of these listed topic areas for FY24 submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exclusions — disallowed cancer research topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional language prohibits the FY24 PRCRP from addressing certain cancers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY24 PRCRP must not address research in melanoma, glioblastoma, or cancers originating in the breast, pancreas, prostate, ovary, kidney, or lung. Applicants researching those excluded disease areas are directed to apply to the individual CDMRP cancer programs that cover those disease areas rather than to the PRCRP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on rare cancers
rubrics_metrics.description: FY24 PRCRP funding may not be used to study rare cancers except in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY24 PRCRP funds must not be used to study rare cancers except for subtypes of the FY24 PRCRP topic areas that are rare by definition. In other words, general rare-cancer research is out of scope unless it is a rare subtype of one of the enumerated FY24 topic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of metastatic cancer for FY24 PRCRP
rubrics_metrics.description: How the PRCRP defines 'metastatic cancer' for the purpose of topic-area inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metastatic cancer is defined as cancer that has spread from its original location to another place in the body, representing stage III and stage IV cancer diagnoses. The page notes that while there is evidence of genetic bases for susceptibility or resistance to metastasis, more research is needed to develop comprehensive understanding—context useful when proposing metastatic-cancer research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pediatric, adolescent, and young adult (AYA) age ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Age group definitions used to scope research targeted to pediatric, adolescent, and young adult cancers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition of adolescents and young adults is derived from the National Cancer Institute. Research should be targeted toward: pediatric (ages 0–14 years), adolescents (ages 15–24 years), and/or young adults (ages 25–39 years). Use these age ranges when proposing studies aimed at these populations.
